## GAMBIA, THE — profile (page 161)
- Header facts: Sub-Saharan Africa; Low-income; IDA; Data as reported (A); Population 2.8 million; GNI 2,560; unit line: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- Total external debt stock, 2025: 1,793; change from 2024: +9.1%.

- Figure 1 Total external debt, 2015–25:
  - Printed start and end values: 586 (2015) and 1,793 (2025).
  - Line shape: generally rising across 2015–25, with modest increases through the middle years and a sharper rise near the end; highest point in 2025. Unlabeled points rise from ≈600 in 2016 to ≈700–900 by the late 2010s/early 2020s, then to ≈1,100 in 2024 before 1,793 in 2025.

- Figure 2 External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:
  - Total external debt: 1,793
  - Public & publicly guaranteed: 1,381
  - Private nonguaranteed: 300
  - Short-term: 112

  - Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type:
    - Multilateral: 1,006
    - Bilateral: 358
    - Private creditors: 17

  - Multilateral:
    - Islamic Dev. Bank: 250
    - IMF credit: 211
    - Other multilateral: 545

  - Bilateral:
    - Saudi Arabia: 135
    - Kuwait: 87
    - Other bilateral: 136

- Figure 3 Debt ratios, 2015–25:
  - External debt / exports: 199%; change: +11.6%; trend: volatile, with a mid-period spike, then decline, ending with a mild uptick by 2025.
  - External debt / GNI: 70%; change: +1.1%; trend: gradual overall increase with some fluctuations; ends near its period high.
  - Debt service / exports: 13%; change: +59.7%; trend: volatile, rising to a peak mid-to-late period, then falling sharply and recovering somewhat by 2025.
  - Debt service / GNI: 5%; change: +44.7%; trend: mostly flat to slightly declining for much of the period, then rising noticeably toward 2025.

- Figure 4 Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:
  - Official creditors:
    - Maturity: 19 yrs
    - Grace period: 3 yrs
    - Interest rate: 1.4%
  - Private creditors:
    - Maturity: ..
    - Grace period: ..
    - Interest rate: ..

- Notes/Source:
  - Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
  - Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
